correctness.rationale: In one-agent S5 equivalence frames, two worlds are bisimilar exactly when own atom color and their E-class color-support sets agree, by direct back-and-forth. Therefore a model is minimal iff each class has distinct colors and distinct classes have different sets of colors. Distinct nonempty subsets of q colors with total incidence n yield n![z^n]prod_{j<=min(n,q)}(1+z^j)^{binom(q,j)} classical simple-hypergraph count. Under uniform Bell partitions, a specified pair merges with probability B_(n-1)/B_n~alpha_n/n, where alpha_n exp(alpha_n)=n. The conditional intra-class possible pair count T satisfies T/(n log n)->1/2 in probability by Bell ratios and second moments; intersecting-pair triple expectation O(n log^2 n). Conditional q-color collision count X has a dependency-graph Poisson approximation with error O((T+H)/q^2), yielding Pois(1/(2theta)) for q/(n log n)->theta>0. Same-color classes with equal supports but no intra-class collisions are negligible by singleton-pair O(log² n/q) and higher-size class O(n²/q²) bounds; this proves minimality limit exp(-1/(2theta)). Pairwise independence of distinct collision indicators yields subcritical whp nonminimality; first-moment and support bounds give supercritical minimality. Direct independent partition/valuation refinement for every n=1..5,q=1..4 matches coefficient enumeration (20 cases).
residual_risks: A binomial coefficient inequality in cross-class bound requires q>=2n in the nondegenerate window/supercritical region, which holds eventually; discrete powers-of-two palettes only have limits along sequences with given ratio. Finite tests cannot establish Poisson asymptotics.
